WhatsApp is developing a new feature that allows users to connect third-party AI agents to the app, chat with them, and instruct them to perform tasks on their behalf. Here are the details.

WhatsApp is developing support for third-party agents

When OpenClaw and similar platforms first went viral, one of the main ways users remotely controlled agents was by connecting them to instant messaging apps.

However, many users subsequently discovered that setting up bots to converse with third-party AI agents on WhatsApp could result in their WhatsApp accounts being banned.

Meanwhile, Telegram rode this wave and has now become one of the primary platforms for users to communicate with or issue commands to agents, which can run on the user's local computer or be deployed in the cloud.

According to WABetaInfo, WhatsApp is introducing native support for third-party AI agents, allowing users to connect agents directly to designated chat windows within the app.

After a user sets up a new bot in WhatsApp, the app generates an API key, which the user can then use to connect an agent to a chat window. WABetaInfo explained: "The specific steps depend on the platform, but most services have a field where users can paste" the API key, enabling direct conversations with third-party agents via WhatsApp.

Below is the report from WABetaInfo:

The site noted that only some Android users currently have access to this new feature, but it is expected to roll out more broadly in the near term. WABetaInfo said WhatsApp's implementation supports up to five agents per account and allows users to customise the name and profile picture for each agent. However, chats with third-party agents do not currently offer end-to-end encryption.
